t: An Ionian island state off Mount Mycale, home of the great sanctuary of Hera and an early Greek naval power.
Under the tyrant Polycrates around 530 BCE it dominated the Aegean and built the harbour mole, the Heraion and the Tunnel of Eupalinos.
Samos was the birthplace of Pythagoras, Epicurus and Aristarchus, who argued that the earth moves around the sun.
dyk: The Tunnel of Eupalinos, 1,036 metres long, was dug from both ends of a mountain at once in the sixth century BCE, and the two teams met almost exactly.
ev: The Samian merchant Colaeus reaches Tartessos in Spain
Polycrates seizes power and builds a fleet of a hundred ships
A Spartan and Corinthian siege of Samos fails after forty days
Polycrates is killed by the Persian satrap Oroetes
Most Samian ships desert at the Battle of Lade
Athens under Pericles crushes the Samian revolt
Athens takes Samos and settles it with Athenian cleruchs
Samos becomes part of the Roman province of Asia

f.predecessor: Carian and Bronze Age settlements of Samos
